A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm heads out for water. "Fetching water. Somebody has to." The pantry won't fill itself.

🔥 The fire settles. the woman in her 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "A dog-shaped silence at the treeline — I put it down today." "No telegraph you can hear. Watch the birds — when they go quiet, the pack is already moving." "The pack circles — nips from the edge, never committing." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. the woman in her 30s, with thick glasses asks "We've been walking past those." the man in his 40s says "The fire feels smaller now."
